summary: Gone King and Queen County lookout: a March 1936 note shows it in service, a 1949 map labels it, and the Forest Fire Lookout Association lists it as gone.

facts.status_note: Forest Fire Lookout Association lists the tower as gone; its entry carries no register number.
facts.agency_note: Source 2 also names the Virginia Department of Forestry on the same page; no source found ties that agency to this tower

events.note: A note dated March 16, 1936 describes a new posting in the Shacklesford fire tower. The page credits it to a CCC company at West Point, Virginia.
A 1949 edition of a map reproduced by Pastmaps labels the Shacklefords Lookout Tower as a prominent landmark.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1936 note spells it Shacklesford; the association's listing and the 1949 map use Shacklefords. Treated as one site.

notes_for_editor: No build date, design, height or fire history was found in the sources reached, so the story starts at the 1936 note. Source 2 is a hobby site reprinting a CCC-era anecdote; the note is secondary and it names a private individual, which the story leaves out. The agency is taken from the heading on that page, not from a statement about this tower, so check it before relying on it. The 1949 label comes from a Pastmaps reprint, not from a scan of the original sheet. The Forest Fire Lookout Association listing is the only register-type record and it gives coordinates only. Access is unknown and no source says what remains at the site.
